title: An LC–MS/MS method for the determination of budesonide and 16α-hydroxyprednisolone in dog plasma
author: Gazzotti, Barbarossa, et al.

steps.title: Add internal standard to plasma
steps.instruction: Pipette 20 µL of BET internal standard solution into 0.5 mL of dog plasma and mix.

steps.title: Activate SPE cartridge
steps.instruction: Condition a Strata‑X SPE cartridge (1 mL, 30 mg, Phenomenex) with 1 mL methanol followed by 1 mL water.

steps.title: Load sample onto cartridge
steps.instruction: Apply the plasma‑internal‑standard mixture to the conditioned cartridge at a flow rate of 2 mL/min.

steps.title: Wash cartridge
steps.instruction: Wash the cartridge with 3 mL of 5 % (v/v) methanol in water.

steps.title: Dry cartridge
steps.instruction: Dry the cartridge under low vacuum for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Elute analytes
steps.instruction: Elute budesonide and 16α‑hydroxyprednisolone with 1.5 mL methanol at 2 mL/min, then remove the eluate completely under vacuum.

steps.title: Evaporate eluate
steps.instruction: Evaporate the collected eluate to dryness under a nitrogen stream while heating at 35 °C.

steps.title: Reconstitute sample
steps.instruction: Re‑dissolve the dried residue in 100 µL of a 1:1 water‑acetonitrile mixture containing 1 % formic acid and vortex for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Transfer to autosampler
steps.instruction: Place the reconstituted extract into an LC‑MS/MS autosampler vial for analysis.

steps.title: Evaluate method specificity
steps.instruction: Analyze ion chromatograms of blank plasma samples from 21 dogs and verify that no interfering peaks co‑elute at the retention times of budesonide, 16α‑HP, or the internal standard.

steps.title: Assess linearity
steps.instruction: Prepare matrix‑matched calibration curves by spiking pooled blank plasma with budesonide and 16α‑HP at 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 5, and 10 ng/mL (freshly prepared on different days). Plot peak‑area ratios (analyte/ BET) versus concentration ratios and perform least‑squares linear regression; accept curves with R² > 0.99.

steps.title: Determine precision and accuracy
steps.instruction: Fortify blank plasma at 0.5, 1, and 5 ng/mL for each analyte. Process 18 spiked samples per level (six per day) over three separate days. Calculate relative standard deviation (CV %) for within‑day repeatability and between‑day reproducibility, and assess accuracy from the measured versus nominal concentrations.

steps.title: Establish limit of quantification
steps.instruction: Identify the lowest concentration giving a signal‑to‑noise ratio > 10 with acceptable precision and accuracy; set the LOQ at 0.25 ng/mL for both budesonide and 16α‑HP.

steps.title: Assess matrix ion suppression
steps.instruction: Perform a post‑column infusion experiment: continuously infuse budesonide and 16α‑HP standards into the MS interface while injecting a blank matrix sample, and monitor for signal suppression across the chromatographic run.

description: An LC–MS/MS method for the quantitative determination of budesonide (BUD) and one of its main metabolite, 16α-hydroxyprednisolone (16α-HP), in dog plasma was developed and validated. The simultaneous quantification of the two molecules, the rapidity and simplicity of the procedure, and the low volume of sample required make the proposed technique suitable for pharmacokinetic studies involving also small-sized dogs. In addition, the developed protocol was employed in a clinical trial on dogs of different breeds, orally treated with BUD once a day for 30 days, demonstrating to be suitable for the purpose [1]. The proposed LC–MS/MS method was validated according to current European guidelines [2], taking into account specificity, linearity, accuracy, precision and limit of quantification (LOQ). The specificity was evaluated checking the ion chromatograms of blank samples collected from 21 dogs and analyzed for potential interfering compounds co-eluting at the specific retention times of the analytes. The linearity of the method was assessed with five-points matrix-matched calibration curves, obtained by spiking pooled blank samples of plasma with standard solutions of BUD and 16α-HP at 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 5 and 10 ng/mL, and freshly prepared during different days. Peak area ratios between each analyte and BET (internal standard) were plotted against their concentration ratios, and a linear regression least square regression model was applied, showing a good linearity (R2 > 0.99). The precision and accuracy of the assay were tested by analyzing blank samples fortified at three concentrations (0.5, 1 and 5 ng/mL) for both analytes. In particular, 18 spiked samples for each level were processed on three different days (six samples per day). The precision was measured as relative standard deviation to the mean (CV%) of both repeatability (within-day) and reproducibility (between-days).
